audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] says his Parrrley out-ranges your Noxious Blast, and whys[2]/whys[3] claim you out-DPS him on levels the chart hands to Gangplank — the page argues with its own chart on three of seven stages.
audit.why: Parrrley is 625 range; Noxious Blast is 850. You out-range his only level-1 poke by 225 units, which is why the chart's Cassiopeia level 1 is right and the why was wrong. Conversely Powder Keg places at 1000 range, outside your 850, which is the real reason levels 3 and 4-5 read Gangplank despite you winning any trade he actually joins.
audit.corrected: whys[0] rewritten around the 625-vs-850 range gap; whys[2] and whys[3] now explain the stage with keg range instead of contradicting it. Charts left untouched.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown block and All-In Windows both tell you to commit on Powder Keg's cooldown. Powder Keg has no cooldown in the ability data — it is charge-based — so the central timing instruction points at a clock that does not exist.
audit.why: Riot's data lists Powder Keg cooldown 0 with a stored-charge mechanic; the ability that does gate this matchup is Remove Scurvy at 22/20/18/16/14s, alongside Parrrley 4.5s and Cannon Barrage 160/140/120s.
audit.corrected: Keg timing replaced with the charge explanation, and the real commit clock moved onto Remove Scurvy 22s with Parrrley and Cannon Barrage numbers added.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike, mid text and whys[4] all promise that Petrifying Gaze locks him for the kill, and wants.foe[1] says Remove Scurvy cleanses Miasma's slow 'and the disabling effect'.
audit.why: Remove Scurvy 'cure[s] crowd control effects and restore[s] Health' — that covers your R stun outright, which is the single biggest interaction on the page and it was never stated. Whether it also clears Miasma's grounding is not established by any local file, so I dropped that half of the claim rather than assert it.
audit.corrected: Every ult line now sequences behind Remove Scurvy: bait its 22s first, then stun. The grounding-cleanse claim removed; the slow-cleanse claim kept because his own description says cure crowd control.

notes: Cannon Barrage carries a derived trueDamage flag in the kit file, but Riot's description only says it slows and damages — I wrote nothing depending on true damage and ignored the resistances-invalidated rule from _missing-interactions.json for that reason.
